$comment: CPE-1594 ratchet, made CASE-granular by CPE-1677. Each entry is ONE test case (`spec` = the spec file's basename, `test` = the it() title, verbatim) that is ALLOWED to fail today. Any OTHER case failing reds the job — including a case inside a spec file that already has entries here, which is exactly the hole CPE-1677 closed (whole-file exemptions meant the other 24 cases in samples.smoke.ts guarded nothing). Removing an entry is one-way: once a listed case passes, the ratchet FAILS until its entry is deleted. A listed `test` that matches NO case in the run also FAILS (titles drift; a rename must not silently drop both the exemption and the coverage). Entries are exact titles, never patterns — a pattern would re-create the blanket exemption this replaced. An entry with "intermittent": true is a case PROVEN to both pass and fail on unchanged code (cite the runs in its reason): it is exempt in both directions, because a coin-flip case would otherwise red every run one way or the other — but it must still exist, and the ratchet prints it with its observed status on every run so it stays visible until it is fixed and deleted. See gui-smoke/README.md 'The ratchet' for the retire procedure.

cases.reason: CPE-1866 (session-per-shard): deterministic on shard 3's real spec ordering — reproduced identically across 3 consecutive CI reruns of the same code (runs ending 32672263270/32677728663/32680942379), always 'element click intercepted' on the fixture row's click, always paired with the two populated-whitespace.smoke.ts entries below in the same run. open-dir.smoke.ts is now the 8th file in a shared session (shard 3), not a fresh app launch, and something upstream in that sequence (near-duplicates.smoke.ts is the file immediately before it) leaves an interceptor in place that CPE-1866's reset (Escape, the app-wide Close-button convention, and — as of this same investigation — a direct `.backdrop` click for an orphaned dialog scrim) did not clear. Not yet root-caused to a specific element: the backdrop fix was a strong, evidenced candidate (60 dialogs share that exact scrim, and NearDuplicatesDialog's own close button is clicked without awaiting its close) but did not clear this on the 3rd rerun, so something else is still standing between the two. Left listed rather than chased further under this ticket's own time-box; a follow-up (CPE-1866's own filed continuation) should re-attempt with a live DOM dump at the failure point.
